message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"3.6","text":"The nature of the one and only God, who made the world, created us, and provided everything, is naturally such that, whenever anyone at all is within the bounds of reverence for God and does not blaspheme his holy spirit, it carries that person’s soul toward him by affection for him, in the form of an innate longing for him. Even if that person is a sinner, after being punished as his deeds deserve, it is in his nature to be saved. If someone denies him or in some other way speaks impiously against him, then reorients himself, he will indeed be punished for the ways in which he sinned against him, but he will be saved, because after turning back he loved him. Perhaps, however, if there is an extraordinary degree of reverence and supplication, he will even be released from punishment, having presented his ignorance together with his reorientation as grounds for forgiveness of the sin. Those, however, who have not reoriented themselves will also meet their end through the punishment of fire, even if they are most devout in every other respect. But, as I said, after being punished with age-long fire for one fifth of a measured age, they will be extinguished. For those who have acted impiously against the eternal and only God can no longer exist forever.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοιαύτη πέφυκεν φύσις","chosen":"is naturally such","rationale":"Preserves the repeated nature language of πέφυκεν and φύσις while allowing the following infinitive to express what this nature characteristically does."},{"source_quote":"αὐτοῦ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα","chosen":"his holy spirit","rationale":"Preserves the possessive expression and descriptive wording without using English capitalization to settle personhood beyond what the Greek itself marks."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τὸ κατ’ ἀξίαν ὧν ἔπραξεν κολασθῆναι σώζεσθαι φύσιν ἔχει","chosen":"after being punished as his deeds deserve, it is in his nature to be saved","rationale":"κατ’ ἀξίαν expresses punishment corresponding to the worth or deserts of the deeds, while φύσιν ἔχει continues the passage’s emphasis on nature."},{"source_quote":"μετανοήσει","chosen":"reorients himself","rationale":"The verb denotes moral-spiritual redirection here. No destination is added because God has already been named, and the distinct ἐπιστρέψας is separately rendered “after turning back.”"},{"source_quote":"συγγνώμης τῆς ἁμαρτίας μετὰ τῆς μετανοίας δεδωκὼς τὴν ἄγνοιαν","chosen":"having presented his ignorance together with his reorientation as grounds for forgiveness of the sin","rationale":"The compact construction presents ignorance and reorientation in relation to pardon. It may alternatively be understood as offering ignorance as an excuse for the sin, but the chosen wording preserves both elements without making ignorance itself absolve him."},{"source_quote":"μεμετρημένου αἰῶνος τὸ πέμπτον πυρὶ αἰωνίῳ κολασθέντες","chosen":"after being punished with age-long fire for one fifth of a measured age","rationale":"“Age-long” preserves the relation between αἰωνίῳ and αἰῶνος and fits the explicitly measured duration; “eternal fire” is a possible lexical alternative, in which case the fire rather than each person’s punishment would be described as eternal."},{"source_quote":"ἀποσβεσθήσονται","chosen":"they will be extinguished","rationale":"Preserves the image of something being put out rather than replacing it with an interpretive abstraction such as “annihilated.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"παντὸς οὐδήποτε ἐντὸς ὅρων θεοσεβείας ὄντος","issue":"The selected print has smooth-breathed οὐδήποτε, which ordinarily means “never” and does not fit the genitive construction with παντός and ὄντος. The context and syntax support the genitive indefinite οὑδήποτε, “of anyone whatsoever.” This is a minimal orthographic correction, not a restoration of missing wording.","proposed_reading":"παντὸς οὑδήποτε ἐντὸς ὅρων θεοσεβείας ὄντος","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἐμφύτου εἰς αὐτὸν ἔρωτος · ἰδέᾳ.","issue":"The confirmed printed raised dot interrupts the natural construction in which ἰδέᾳ governs the preceding genitive phrase. Treating it as sentence-final would leave ἰδέᾳ isolated before the full stop. The translation therefore treats it as anomalous internal editorial punctuation and attaches ἰδέᾳ to the preceding words.","proposed_reading":"ἐμφύτου εἰς αὐτὸν ἔρωτος ἰδέᾳ.","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"3.7","text":"Impiety toward him, then, is for a person who is within the discourse of reverence for God to die saying that there is another god besides the one who truly exists—whether speaking of that other as superior, as inferior, or in any way whatever. For the one who truly exists is this one, whose form the human body bears and for whose sake heaven and all the stars, though superior in essence, submitted to serve the one inferior in essence because of the superior one’s form. God has benefited the human being so greatly beyond all others that, having loved the benefactor because of the multitude of benefits, the human being might, by that very love, be preserved into the second age.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ τῆς θεοσεβείας λόγῳ ὄντα","chosen":"a person who is within the discourse of reverence for God","rationale":"λόγος may denote discourse, teaching, or profession. “Discourse” preserves the wording without reducing it solely to either private belief or formal religious office."},{"source_quote":"τελευτᾶν λέγοντα","chosen":"to die saying","rationale":"τελευτᾶν can mean “die” or “come to an end,” while a possible alternative is “end by saying” or “finally say.” The death sense is chosen because the surrounding argument concerns what a person maintains until death and the next section again speaks of dying under a charge."},{"source_quote":"οὗ τὴν μορφὴν τὸ ἀνθρώπου βαστάζει σῶμα","chosen":"whose form the human body bears","rationale":"μορφή is rendered “form” rather than harmonized with the more familiar theological term “image,” and βαστάζει retains the concrete idea of bearing."},{"source_quote":"κατ’ οὐσίαν κρείττονες ὄντες, τῷ κατ’ οὐσίαν χείρονι","chosen":"though superior in essence, submitted to serve the one inferior in essence","rationale":"The repeated κατ’ οὐσίαν is preserved symmetrically. The Greek leaves the inferior recipient grammatically substantive; the context identifies it with the human being, but the translation does not insert that identification into the phrase."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸ πλῆθος τῶν εὐεργεσιῶν","chosen":"because of the multitude of benefits","rationale":"The preposition εἰς marks the multitude of benefits as the ground or occasion for loving the benefactor; “in response to” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν δεύτερον αἰῶνα διασωθῆναι","chosen":"be preserved into the second age","rationale":"διασῴζω can mean to save, preserve safely, or bring safely through. “Preserved into” retains both the saving sense and the stated destination."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.8","text":"Affection for God on the part of human beings is therefore sufficient for salvation. The evil one, however, knowing that we are eager to sow in the souls of those from the nations who are about to believe the immortality-giving affection that human beings direct toward the one and only God, himself strives, while possessing against the ignorant a weapon sufficient for destruction, to sow the notion of many gods, or even of one as superior, so that, having conceived and become jointly convinced of things that are unlawful, after dying as though under a charge of adultery they may be cast out of his kingdom.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αὐτάρκης οὖν εἰς σωτηρίαν","chosen":"is therefore sufficient for salvation","rationale":"αὐτάρκης denotes being sufficient or adequate in oneself; the rendering preserves the passage’s explicit claim about affection and salvation."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἀπὸ ἐθνῶν πιστεύειν μέλλουσιν","chosen":"those from the nations who are about to believe","rationale":"Retains the source’s “from the nations” wording rather than automatically importing the conventional label “Gentiles.”"},{"source_quote":"τὴν ἀθανατοποιὸν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀνθρώπων στοργήν","chosen":"the immortality-giving affection that human beings direct toward him","rationale":"ἀθανατοποιός describes the affection as producing immortality, not merely as immortal in quality; πρὸς αὐτόν marks its direction."},{"source_quote":"πολλῶν θεῶν ἢ καὶ ἑνὸς ὡς κρείττονος","chosen":"many gods, or even one as superior","rationale":"The ellipsis after ἑνός is retained: one god is implied, but the Greek does not restate whom that one is superior to."},{"source_quote":"συλλαβόντες","chosen":"having conceived","rationale":"The verb can mean “grasped” or “accepted,” but “conceived” continues the preceding image of seed being sown and anticipates the adultery image."},{"source_quote":"συνπεισθέντες ἃ μὴ θέμις","chosen":"become jointly convinced of things that are unlawful","rationale":"The συν- element indicates shared persuasion, though the Greek does not specify whether the sharing is with the evil one or with others who accept the notion. “Come to share belief in” is a viable alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῆς αὐτοῦ βασιλείας","chosen":"his kingdom","rationale":"The pronoun is preserved. The argument points to God’s kingdom, although the evil one is the nearest explicitly named masculine referent."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.9","text":"Everyone, therefore, is worthy of exclusion who has so much as wished to hear anything of that kind against God’s sole rule. But if anyone, emboldened by the Scriptures, dares even to hear something directed against God, let him first reflect with me on this: if someone constructs for himself a plausible doctrine in whatever way he wishes and then studies them closely, he will be able to cite from them many testimonies in support of the doctrine he fashioned. How, then, can anyone confidently rely on these writings against God, when everyone’s chosen view can be found in them?","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῆς θεοῦ μοναρχίας","chosen":"God’s sole rule","rationale":"μοναρχία denotes rule by one. “Sole rule” preserves its theological force more transparently than the modern political term “monarchy.”"},{"source_quote":"αὐτὸ μόνον κἂν ἀκοῦσαί τι τοιοῦτον θελήσας","chosen":"who has so much as wished to hear anything of that kind","rationale":"The wording stresses that the mere willingness even to listen is enough for the stated condemnation."},{"source_quote":"ὡς γραφαῖς τεθαρρηκὼς","chosen":"emboldened by the Scriptures","rationale":"γραφαί may be rendered generically as “writings,” but the continuing references to scriptural testimonies and passages support “the Scriptures” here."},{"source_quote":"εὔλογον ἑαυτῷ δόγμα ὡς βούλεται ἀναπλάσῃ","chosen":"constructs for himself a plausible doctrine in whatever way he wishes","rationale":"εὔλογον can mean reasonable or plausible. “Plausible” suits the argument that a person first fabricates a position and then seeks supporting texts."},{"source_quote":"αὐταῖς ἐνκύψῃ","chosen":"studies them closely","rationale":"ἐγκύπτω literally suggests bending over or peering into something and idiomatically denotes close examination."},{"source_quote":"ἐν αἷς ἡ πάντων βουλὴ εἰσευρίσκεται","chosen":"when everyone’s chosen view can be found in them","rationale":"βουλή can mean counsel, purpose, will, or opinion. The context concerns finding textual support for whatever doctrine one wants, so “chosen view” is adopted; “everyone’s counsel” would be more formally literal but less clear in context."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"3.10","text":"For instance, Simon, who is to debate with us tomorrow, dares to argue publicly against God’s sole rule, intending to bring forward many statements from the Scriptures themselves to the effect that there are many gods and that a certain one—not the one who created the world—is higher than the latter; and correspondingly he can furnish written proofs. We too can clearly point out many passages from the same Scriptures showing that this one, the one who created the world, is the one God, and that “there is no other except him.” Yet if anyone wishes to speak in some other way, he too will be able to provide proofs from them, in whatever way he wishes and about whatever he wishes. For the Scriptures say everything, so that none of those who search for the truth ungratefully may find it, but instead may find what he wants, while the truth is reserved for the grateful. Gratitude consists in preserving intact one’s affection for the one responsible for our existence.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"αὐτίκα γοῦν","chosen":"For instance","rationale":"The phrase introduces Simon as an immediate illustration of the preceding general claim; “at any rate, immediately” would preserve the particles more formally."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ μοναρχίας","chosen":"against God’s sole rule","rationale":"Renders μοναρχία as the rule of one rather than using a modern political label."},{"source_quote":"πολλὰς ἐξ αὐτῶν τῶν γραφῶν φωνὰς ἐνεγκεῖν","chosen":"to bring forward many statements from the Scriptures themselves","rationale":"φωναί literally means voices or utterances; “statements” fits citations taken from written texts while preserving their asserted content."},{"source_quote":"εἷς δέ τις οὐχ ὁ τὸν κόσμον κτίσας τούτου ἀνώτερος","chosen":"a certain one—not the one who created the world—is higher than the latter","rationale":"The chosen syntax understands τούτου as the world-creator and the certain other god as superior to him. The compressed word order permits some attachment uncertainty, which “the latter” preserves without supplying a name."},{"source_quote":"καὶ ὁμῶς τὰς ἀποδείξεις ἐγγράφους ἔχει παρασχεῖν","chosen":"and correspondingly he can furnish written proofs","rationale":"The printed ὁμῶς means “equally” or “likewise,” hence “correspondingly.” “Nevertheless” would normally represent differently accented ὅμως and is not adopted."},{"source_quote":"πολλὰς περικοπὰς","chosen":"many passages","rationale":"περικοπαί are portions or sections cut from a larger text, naturally rendered here as scriptural passages."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀγνωμόνως ζητούντων","chosen":"those who search for the truth ungratefully","rationale":"ἀγνωμόνως may also mean without judgment or unreasonably. The author’s immediate definition of εὐγνωμοσύνη as preserving affection for one’s benefactor supports the gratitude sense here."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἀληθοῦς τοῖς εὐγνώμοσιν τετηρημένου","chosen":"while the truth is reserved for the grateful","rationale":"εὐγνώμων can mean right-minded, fair, or grateful. “Grateful” maintains the contrast with ἀγνωμόνως and anticipates the next sentence’s definition."},{"source_quote":"εὐγνωμοσύνη δέ ἐστιν τὸ τὴν πρὸς τὸν τοῦ εἶναι ἡμᾶς αἴτιον ἀποσώζειν στοργήν","chosen":"Gratitude consists in preserving intact one’s affection for the one responsible for our existence","rationale":"ἀποσώζειν conveys keeping or preserving safely and intact. “Gratitude” fits the benefactor relationship expressed by affection toward the cause of human existence, though “right-mindedness” remains a lexical alternative."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
